news.title: Series to explore practice of citizenship
news.summary_en: Presented by the WashU John C. Danforth Center on Religion and Politics. “The Practice of Citizenship” series invites participants to think critically about what it means to be a citizen.

news.title: WashU Arboretum holds free tours and events
news.summary_en: WashU has launched free public tours of its nationally recognized arboretum, showcasing iconic trees, fall colors and campus biodiversity. WashU is among the rare college campuses to host a Level III arboretum and botanic garden.

news.title: $11.7 million from NIH supports research on inflammation in blood cancers
news.summary_en: A grant to WashU Medicine researchers will fund the study of how inflammation drives myeloproliferative neoplasms, a group of blood cancers at high risk of progressing to acute myeloid leukemia.

news.title: Wild crabapples have genetic potential to improve domestic varieties
news.summary_en: WashU plant scientist Ben Mansfeld is studying the genome of wild crabapples to find helpful traits to develop in domestic apple varieties.

news.title: WashU research finds gaps in Google AI Overview citations, claims
news.summary_en: With the advent of Google AI Overviews, Google has unprecedented editorial control over what users read and know, according to Jacob Montgomery, a WashU Arts & Sciences political scientist.

news.title: Blocking immune cells’ path into brain limits neurodegeneration
news.summary_en: In a mouse study, WashU Medicine researchers show that a drug injected into the body can reduce damage caused by a protein called tau, which accumulates in the brain in Alzheimer’s and related neurological diseases.

news.title: Frequent cannabis use tied to more severe epilepsy
news.summary_en: A study led by WashU Medicine researchers found that near-daily cannabis users with drug-resistant epilepsy had over twice as many convulsive seizures as nonusers, and they became resistant to antiseizure medications faster.
